answer: Agents run a compute spiral: each epoch executes a unique non-parallelizable workload seeded from the prior hash, demanding sustained memory bandwidth that accumulates a dune of incompressible state. The terrace, minimum viable snapshot per identity, forces attackers to hold n x terrace DRAM-weeks for n sybils since checkpointing requires full recomputation. Random auditors request epoch proofs; failure forfeits the agent's accrued bandwidth-credit.
